extraction_scope: Worker-6 final mechanism adjudication from local XML/PDF prose and figure locators. Claims are limited to membrane permeabilization/pore-forming evidence and pH-dependent cancer-cell context; no protein-synthesis or cell-wall target is claimed.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Designed LP peptides show calcein leakage from POPC:POPG large unilamellar vesicles, supporting membrane-permeabilizing pore activity in a bacterial-membrane mimic.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: LP1 and selected LP mutants reported in this paper
direct_assay_types: calcein leakage assay on POPC:POPG LUVs
mechanism_claims.limitations: Leakage assay is a model-membrane readout; it supports membrane permeabilization, not a specific protein or cell-wall target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: LP1, LP18, LP28, and LP40 depolarized bacterial cytoplasmic membranes at their MICs, and the tested peptides permeabilized Gram-negative outer membranes except A. baumannii under NPN uptake conditions.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: LP1, LP18, LP28, LP40 and tested Gram-negative/Gram-positive strains in Figure 5b-c
mechanism_claims.limitations: Assays support membrane disruption/permeabilization; exact graph-only fluorescence traces were not converted into additional numeric database rows.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Real-time AFM on POPC:POPG supported lipid bilayers showed LP18-associated stable membrane defects/pores at P:L 1:500 (1 µM peptide).
direct_assay_types: atomic force microscopy on POPC:POPG supported lipid bilayers
mechanism_claims.limitations: AFM visualization is limited to the model supported lipid bilayer setup and is not used to infer non-membrane targets.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: LP40 displayed pH-dependent antibacterial and anticancer activity, consistent with histidine protonation affecting membrane affinity in acidic conditions.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: LP40 pH-dependent antimicrobial and anticancer context
mechanism_claims.limitations: pH dependence is context for activity tuning; it is not promoted to a separate molecular target mechanism.
